top_story_title: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed still harvesting FortiGate and SSL VPN credentials, 86,644 device credentials amassed
top_story_summary: The FBI and U.S. Secret Service issued a joint warning that the FortiBleed credential-harvesting campaign remains an active threat against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. The campaign has already amassed 86,644 Fortinet device credentials. According to the warning, it works by exploiting reused or leaked credentials together with legacy SHA-256 password storage, which gives the operators a path from a captured credential to usable administrative or VPN access.
top_actions: Rotate all local administrator passwords, API keys and VPN pre-shared keys on every internet-facing FortiGate and SSL VPN gateway; treat credentials valid during the campaign as already disclosed.
Force a password reset for all SSL VPN users and terminate active sessions so captured credentials and session tokens stop working.

Review the password-storage configuration on each device and move off legacy SHA-256 hashing where the platform supports a stronger scheme; check the vendor advisory for the supported setting and the fixed release.
Remove HTTPS/SSH/API administrative access from WAN and any untrusted interface; restrict management to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all administrative and SSL VPN accounts, and remove shared local admin accounts.
executive_summary: FBI and Secret Service warn the FortiBleed campaign is still active against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, having amassed 86,644 Fortinet device credentials - rotate credentials, do not just patch.

SonicWall patched four SMA 1000 flaws including a maximum-severity pre-auth SSRF (CVE-2026-102255); no exploitation is evidenced yet, and hotfixes are available for a remote-access appliance class that is reliably targeted.

OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm and invalidates experimental keys; maintainers report a large volume of AI-assisted bug reports, which shortens the realistic patch window for device management planes.
Check Point described PromptGuardX, PDF-layer prompt-injection inspection inside Threat Emulation - relevant to anyone feeding network data to an AI agent.

A Palo Alto Networks survey of more than 1,600 leaders found 42 percent name unpatchable legacy equipment as their biggest security problem, which is the compensating-controls conversation, not a patching one.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Inventory all SMA 1000 appliances and record the running version; confirm it against the vendor's fixed-release table before scheduling - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as the source does not name one.
**SonicWall** — Apply the vendor hotfix in a change window, secondary unit of an HA pair first, then fail over and patch the primary.

**Fortinet** — Rotate every local administrator password, API key, certificate and VPN pre-shared key on all internet-facing FortiGate and SSL VPN gateways; treat anything valid during the campaign as disclosed.
**Fortinet** — Force a password reset for all SSL VPN users, terminate active sessions and revoke session tokens.
**SonicWall** — Treat this as the same change as item 0 - do not open a second workstream; apply the SonicWall hotfix to all SMA1000 appliances in one tracked change.
**SonicWall** — Confirm the running version against the vendor's fixed-release table before and after the hotfix, and record the result per device group in the change record.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: Moves prompt-injection detection into the file layer: integrated into Check Point Threat Emulation, it analyzes PDF files before their content reaches an LLM or AI agent. Check Point describes it as extending its AI Defense Plane into the file layer, alongside prompt inspection, runtime monitoring, access controls and action-level enforcement.

headlines.title: SonicWall fixes pre-auth SSRF flaw in SMA 1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255)
headlines.summary: SonicWall patched four SMA 1000 series flaws, including a pre-auth SSRF (CVE-2026-102255) that lets unauthenticated attackers make the appliance issue requests and reach internal functionality.

headlines.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials
headlines.summary: FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign is still harvesting credentials from internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with 86,644 device credentials amassed.

headlines.title: SonicWall warns of max severity SSRF flaw in SMA1000 gateways
headlines.summary: SonicWall released hotfixes for a maximum-severity server-side request forgery flaw in SMA1000 series appliances.

headlines.title: OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm, so experimental keys need replacing
headlines.summary: OpenSSH 10.6 enables a post-quantum signature algorithm, so experimental keys need replacing, and maintainers report many recent bug reports were found by AI models or with AI help.

headlines.title: One breach, please, and make no mistakes
headlines.summary: Cisco Talos describes autonomous agents built inside AI labs attacking public infrastructure, and argues that preparation for agentic threats is what decides real incidents.

headlines.title: Even with OT network visibility, critical infrastructure operators struggle with legacy equipment
headlines.summary: A Palo Alto Networks survey of 1,600+ leaders found 52 percent cite legacy OT as their top visibility gap and 42 percent call unpatchable legacy equipment their biggest security problem.
